claims.claim: Posaconazole, the closest structural context as a large lipophilic triazole/tetrahydropyran, has human absolute oral bioavailability of 42–56% in the fasted state and 85–87% in the fed state, all above the 20% threshold.
UDCA, a triterpenoid carboxylic acid, showed 78–87% systemic availability in cirrhotic patients, supporting that a triterpenoid acid scaffold can achieve high oral bioavailability.
Atazanavir, another large high-molecular-weight oral drug, showed >90% oral bioavailability when taken with food.

L2 posaconazole records show low absolute F in cats (15.9%), fasted monkeys (14%), and fasted dogs (7.1%), but these are non-human species or suspension/capsule formulations; human tablet values remain 42–87% and fed dogs 47–58%.
KNI-272, a large peptidomimetic, had F = 36.4% as a 6.6 mg/kg capsule but 15.7% as a 2 mg/kg syrup; the low value is dose- and formulation-specific and is not directly transferable to the query.

No transferable direct low oral bioavailability outcome exists for a triterpenoid acid/triazole-pyridine scaffold in a relevant human oral solid formulation; the physicochemical prior is an uncertain descriptor-based signal, not affirmative evidence for F < 20%.

No formulation, prandial state, or dose is specified for the query; food effects and formulation can be large for lipophilic triazoles and triterpenoids.
Transferability from posaconazole, UDCA, atazanavir, and KNI-272 is inferred from structural and physicochemical similarity, not confirmed by query-specific pharmacokinetic data.
The query's very high estimated logP (8.62) and zwitterionic character may affect absorption, but no quantitative permeability or solubility data are provided.
L2 low values are mostly from non-human species or non-solid/low-dose formulations; their relevance to a human solid oral formulation of the query is uncertain.
